name: Waldorf Astoria Jeddah Qasr Al Sharq
positioning: A former palace on North Corniche Road in Jeddah, now a Waldorf Astoria with gold accents, Italian furnishings and a mix of modern and Arabic design
best_for: Travelers who want a suite with a Red Sea view and butler service
Women looking for a spa reserved for women

facts.text: The hotel is on North Corniche Road in Jeddah.
The hotel is adorned with gold accents, Italian furnishings and crystal.
Rooms and suites mix modern and Arabic interior design.
Each suite has golden ceilings, marble bathrooms and a view of the Red Sea.
The hotel has two restaurants: Mataam Al Sharq for Middle Eastern cuisine and Aromi for Italian cuisine.
Al Shurfa Lounge serves coffee, tea and pastries for a quick breakfast.
Al Shurfa Lounge serves afternoon tea.
The spa offers an AquaMed Hydrotherapy bed.
Spa treatments include custom spa rituals, deep cleansing facials and Thai massages.
The spa menu includes Clarins facials.
The hotel offers personalized butler service and an EV charging station.
The hotel has meeting rooms equipped with a business center.

highlights.text: The hotel was originally built as a palace and then converted into a Waldorf Astoria hotel.
The Qasr al Sharq suite covers half of an entire floor.
The Qasr al Sharq suite includes two master bedrooms, a formal majlis and a private health club.
Guests arrive under a three-story Swarovski chandelier.
Conde Nast Traveler reports the hotel was designed by the firm behind Dubai's Burj Al Arab.

considerations.text: The spa is reserved for women.
WhataHotel notes no alcoholic beverages are served on property, in keeping with Saudi regulations.
